forces: The admission boundary must close synchronously at the exact moment shutdown is initiated so no concurrent submission can be accepted after it, without any locking primitive.

Deadline-bounded draining must produce an exact accepted/completed/abandoned accounting even though JavaScript promises cannot be forcibly cancelled, and must never report abandoned work as delivered.
Repeated or concurrent shutdown calls must be idempotent and must never re-drain or double-count already-reported work.

The mechanism must reuse the delivery layer's own established shutdown-timer pattern (cancellable, unref'd) rather than inventing a second one, and must remain independent of what the wrapped delivery operation is.

candidate_approaches.summary: A boolean admission flag checked synchronously in submit(), plus a Set of in-flight promises drained via Promise.race against a cancellable deadline timer mirroring security-audit-sdk-core's createShutdownTimeout, with the shutdown report memoized for idempotency.

approach-alternative-implement-delivery-.reason: Requiring every wrapped operation to accept and cooperatively honor an AbortSignal would couple this generic composing module to a cancellation contract none of the existing handoff, retry, or backpressure modules implement, and the issue explicitly excludes guaranteeing anything about persistence after cancellation — abandonment-by-accounting satisfies the acceptance criteria without that added surface.

evidence_ids: new-admission-rejected test: a submission attempted synchronously right after shutdown() is called is rejected without invoking the operation
concurrent-admission-boundary test asserts no window exists for an admission to cross the boundary
empty-drain test: shutdown resolves without waiting for the deadline and reports zero abandoned
deadline-expiry test: exact accepted/completed/abandoned counts when operations remain outstanding
never-silently-dropped test: an abandoned operation's own submit() call still resolves once it settles
idempotency test: repeated and concurrent shutdown() calls return the identical report object

security_justification.audit_integrity: Shutdown never reports an abandoned operation as delivered or completed; the accepted/completed/abandoned counts are derived directly from the tracked Set's membership, not from an independently-maintained flag that could drift.
security_justification.authentication_or_authorization: The module performs no authentication or authorization; it gates admission by lifecycle phase only, independent of caller or credential identity.
security_justification.authority_provenance: The module does not read, construct, or forward any event identity; it only tracks in-flight promises and forwards whatever the wrapped operation returns.
security_justification.concurrency: The admission flag is checked synchronously with no `await` before it, which is atomic under Node's run-to-completion semantics; the memoized shutdown promise guarantees exactly one drain regardless of how many callers call shutdown() concurrently.
security_justification.confidentiality: The module never inspects, stores, or logs the wrapped operation's arguments or result beyond forwarding it to the original submit() caller; the shutdown report contains only numeric counts.
security_justification.cryptography: No cipher, key, signature, hash, or TLS configuration is introduced or touched.
security_justification.error_disclosure: A wrapped operation's rejection propagates to its own submit() caller unchanged; the shutdown report and the rejected_shutting_down result carry no operation-specific text beyond this module's own bounded construction-time TypeError.
security_justification.external_security_integration: The module adds no network client, security service, credential store, or external runtime integration; it wraps a caller-supplied function and an injected timer provider.
security_justification.fail_posture: New admission fails closed immediately once shutdown starts; a deadline that expires with outstanding work fails to an explicit abandoned count rather than silently reporting success or hanging indefinitely.
security_justification.lifecycle: The module's only resource is the in-memory Set of in-flight promises and one cancellable, unref'd deadline timer per shutdown call; the timer is always cancelled on the winning drain path so no dangling resource remains referenced by this module.
security_justification.mutation_ownership: The change is bounded to the new shutdown module, its export, tests, documentation, and the owning OpenSpec artifacts and capability specification.
security_justification.privacy_transformation: The module performs no personal-data collection, transformation, or retention; it never inspects the wrapped operation's payload.
security_justification.resource_retention: In-flight tracking is bounded to operations admitted during this module's lifetime and is cleared as each settles; no operation result, argument, or timer is retained after the shutdown report is produced.
security_justification.retry_or_redelivery: The module never retries; it wraps whatever operation it is given exactly once per submit call and reports that call's own outcome, independent of shutdown's own accounting.
security_justification.trust_boundary: The only attacker-controlled pressure this module answers is submission timing relative to shutdown; a submission attempted after the boundary is rejected deterministically rather than admitted, queued, or silently dropped.
